messages:
Maya: heads-up — customer acme-inc (private VPC) reports intermittent 502s to /v1/generate when traffic goes through their corporate LB. LB logs show TLS handshake failures. ticket C-82415.
Devon: can you paste the client-side error? is it 'no shared cipher' or 'handshake failure'?
Maya: customer paste: 'curl: (35) error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number' and LB: 'SSL handshake failed: no cipher match (client hello ECDSA only)'. They also ran openssl s_client: ```openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.example:443 -servername api.redwood.example -alpn h2 -tls1_2``` and it returns no shared cipher.
Kai: are they terminating TLS at the LB and re-encrypting to upstream? that pattern often exposes cipher/keytype mismatches.
Maya: yes, they terminate and re-encrypt to upstream. Upstream uses an RSA cert. Their LB profile is supposedly ECDSA-strict per corp policy.
Devon: ok. two likely problems: 1) LB configured to only accept ECDSA-based ciphers but upstream cert is RSA -> no common keytype; 2) TLS version mismatch (tls1.3 disabled at LB). Ask for LB cipher profile + cert type. Also ask them to try forcing TLS1.3 locally: ```openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.example:443 -tls1_3 -ciphersuites TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256```
Maya: they ran tls1.3 test -> still handshake failure. their LB snippet: ```ssl-profile {
  protocols TLS1.2;
  ciphers 'ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256';
  certs ecdsa_only
}``` they admit they rolled out strict profile to satisfy enterprise crypto scanner.
Devon: that explains it. if their LB only advertises ECDSA ciphers and upstream certs are RSA, no cipher will be selected. Short-term options: 1) re-enable ECDHE-RSA ciphers on the LB; 2) allow TLS1.3 on the LB (it negotiates differently and supports mixed key exchanges); 3) upload a matching ECDSA cert on the upstream path. Also can offer workaround: route traffic through a proxy that presents an RSA-compatible profile or use Dedicated with private egress if customer wants us to handle egress.
Kai: reproduced locally by deploying an F5 with same profile, connected to an RSA-only origin — same handshake abort. tcpdump shows ClientHello EC curves present but server cert keytype=RSA and F5 cipher selection filters out RSA-based ECDHE.
Maya: sent suggested steps to customer: 1) temporarily add ECDHE-RSA ciphers to the profile; 2) or add RSA certs to relevant upstream pools; 3) run this test and paste output: ```openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.example:443 -cipher 'ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256' -servername api.redwood.example```
oncall-bot: escalated to eng-runtime (ticket C-82415)
Maya: customer applied ECDHE-RSA -> confirmed 200 responses, no more 502s. they're scheduling a permanent profile change to support mixed key types.
Devon: great. I'll add an internal KB: "Strict ECDSA-only LB profiles can break re-encryption to RSA-only upstreams; recommend enabling ECDHE-RSA fallback or TLS1.3." Also note a suggested troubleshooting checklist (collect s_client output, LB cipher profile, cert key type, packet capture). :memo: 
Kai: adding a small config snippet we can share with customers for F5/AWS ALB to avoid breakage.
Maya: updating ticket and closing this Slack thread. thanks team :thumbsup:
